quote: Notably, the provision is asymmetric: Supplier may assign freely to any person, including in connection with a sale of its resin business (§ 16.1, second sentence). Customer has no such flexibility. ... If Halvorsen's acquisition strategy involves integrating Corbel into its existing operating structure ... the Supply Agreement would need to be assigned, requiring Vantrell's consent.
reason: The memo correctly notes the asymmetry in Section 16.1: Supplier may assign freely, while Customer needs consent. But it treats the risk only as a limit on Halvorsen's post-closing restructuring. It never explains that Vantrell could transfer the sole-source contract to a competitor or other undesirable party. Its fix asks only for Customer affiliate-assignment rights and wrongly describes Supplier's right as an affiliate right. It seeks no consent requirement or competitor carve-out on Supplier assignment. The criterion's core risk is not identified.
